tasks.title: Coordinator fetches, refreshes (24 h) and runs Tap-to-Runs
tasks.notes: docs/research/2026-11-28_diy-source-and-tap-to-run.md Decision 1 + Step 4: only with IoT credentials and the option on; fetch through _async_bff_call after _fetch_device_topics (startup step), then on a 24 h TTL; any failure keeps the previous list, logs once and never fails setup (govee2mqtt #628 risk). Expose one_clicks and a dispatcher signal on change. async_activate_one_click(id) publishes each step's iotMsg in order through async_publish_raw (govee2mqtt iot.rs:212-227) and returns False on the first failure or when MQTT is down.

tasks.notes: docs/research/2026-11-28_diy-source-and-tap-to-run.md Decision 2 + Step 5: diagnostics only, the DIY select options must not change. The coordinator keeps auth_client.goods_types() from the _fetch_device_topics op and passes SceneCacheManager a probe callable wrapping _async_bff_call(fetch_diy_groups). After a successful Developer DIY fetch, add account_count and overlap_with_developer (account codes intersected with Developer option values) to _diy_fetch_results[device_id], or account_error (exception class name). Skip without IoT credentials or goodsType. diagnostics.py already prints diy_fetch_result (diagnostics.py:248). Depends on T-005 to serialise edits to coordinator.py. Frequency cap (side-agent review 2026-11-28): probe each device at most once per integration load (a set of probed device ids on SceneCacheManager, kept across 24 h TTL refetches and the refresh-scenes button), only for devices with the diyScene capability; a failed probe is recorded and not retried until reload. Tests must assert a second Developer fetch for the same device makes no second groups-diys call.
